predecessors.note: One kingdom on the Thuringii page; the 475/476 cut is Cliopatria's.

land.text: the Thuringian kingdom, conquered by the Franks in 531-532: Theuderic I 'took control of the Unstrut region'

successors.note: Thuringii page: 'conquered by the Franks in 531-532'; the Cliopatria row runs to 533. Cliopatria's Duchy of Thuringia row starts only in 567; the Saxon share of the old kingdom is not on the page.

keyframe_review.note: 40,557 km2 for 476-522, the same shape as the 469 row (9.18-12.30 E, 49.25-51.92 N), Thuringia between the Harz and the Thuringian forest. The Thuringii page: the kingdom 'reached its territorial peak in the first half of the sixth' century before it 'was conquered by the Franks in 531-532', and Theoderic wrote to 'Herminafrid, king of the Thuringians' (493-507 letters); it also reports raids near Passau and Linz in the 460s-470s, a Danube presence the shape does not draw. No area figure on the page, so no infobox comparison.

correction.text: the Thuringian kingdom's shape unchanged from 476, held 523-532 (Cliopatria's 533 end moved to the 531-532 Frankish conquest)

keyframe_review.note: The shape is unchanged (40,557 km2, identical to 476) and the page gives nothing for 523 (the Cliopatria break is unexplained; Herminafrid's killing of his brother Berthachar and alliance with Austrasia is undated). The years change: the page has the Franks conquer the kingdom in 531-532, one year before Cliopatria's 533, so the keyframe runs 523-532.

region.text: Thuringia, between the Harz and the Thuringian forest

ledger.note: 476: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Thuringia row begins on the land of its Thuringian states row (469-475). The Thuringii page dates no founding in 476 ('established an empire in the late fifth century'); the year is the row seam, confidence 1.

region.text: Thuringia, fought over between Herminafrid and Theuderic I of Austrasia

ledger.note: 531: the Franks of Austrasia attack Thuringia. 'It reached its territorial peak in the first half of the sixth before it was conquered by the Franks in 531-532'; 'Theuderic I defeated Herminafrid in two battles and took control of the Unstrut region'. The page dates no battle; 531 opens the page's conquest window (confidence 2).

region.text: Thuringia, fought over between Herminafrid and Theuderic I of Austrasia

ledger.note: 532: the fighting ends with the kingdom conquered. 'conquered by the Franks in 531-532'; Herminafrid 'died at Zulpich as the result of an assassination attempt'.

region.text: the Thuringian kingdom, the Unstrut region and Thuringia

ledger.note: 532: Thuringia passes to the Franks. 'conquered by the Franks in 531-532' (Thuringii page); the page does not mention a partition with the Saxons or an annexation year later than 532.

region.text: the Thuringian kingdom, annexed by the Franks

ledger.note: 532: the Thuringian kingdom ends. 'conquered by the Franks in 531-532'; Cliopatria's row runs to 533, one year later. Later: 'Under the leadership of Alboin, a large group of Thuringi joined the Lombards on their migration into Italy' (568).

wars.name: Frankish conquest of Thuringia
wars.outcome: Frankish victory: 'Theuderic I defeated Herminafrid in two battles and took control of the Unstrut region'; the kingdom was 'conquered by the Franks in 531-532'.
wars.note: The page does not name the battles (the 'Battle of Burgscheidungen' article returned URL_NOT_FOUND), the Saxon allies or the partition; Herminafrid had 'allied himself with the Frankish king of Austrasia' after killing his brother Berthachar. Theoderic the Great's niece married Herminafrid ('for her marriage', an embassy in 493-507).

certainty.note: A tribal kingdom with no recorded frontier; the early forms may have reached the Rhine and northern Bavaria.

notes: Cliopatria rows: Kingdom of Thuringia 476-533 (two shapes, both 40,557 km2, the second from 523 with no cause on the pages) and the earlier Thuringian states row 469-475 (thuringian-states dossier). Both are one kingdom; merge under thuringian-states if the project wants one colour. The Cliopatria Wikipedia title 'Basina of Thuringia' is a person page; the Thuringii article is the state's. End year: the page says 531-532, Cliopatria 533; this dossier ends 532 and the 523 keyframe is cut to 523-532. A reviewer who prefers the Cliopatria year can move the dissolve to 533. No capital and no ruler list: the pages name Bisinus (not on the page opened), Basina, Herminafrid, Berthachar and Baderich without reign dates. Not on the pages: the partition with the Saxons, the battles of 531-532 (Unstrut, Burgscheidungen), the Elbe-Saale frontier, the origin of the 523 break. Counterpart saxons is therefore not used. Cliopatria's Duchy of Thuringia (567-723, eu-06) is the later duchy. Page budget: Thuringii and Basina of Thuringia, plus the failed 'Battle of Burgscheidungen'.
